clue.text: O for Officer?

parts.note: the letter O stands second in the word 'command', and a deputy officer holds that rank below the commander

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'O' as a letter: in the word COMMAND it is the second letter. The '?' signals the pun on a deputy's rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy who ranks just below the commander is an officer, and the letter O sits in position two of 'command'.

clue.text: In various parts, classic tours thus restricted by passport?

indicators.note: to tour something is to go all the way round it, so the first piece surrounds what follows

parts.note: a classic work on a grand scale is an epic

indicators.note: a word restricted by another is hemmed in by it, so the next piece holds this one

parts.note: a passport is a form of identification, ID
thus means so

explanation.surface: A classic tour hampered by passport restrictions takes place in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'restricted by' wraps the passport around 'thus', and 'tours' wraps the classic around that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic happens in separate instalments, like a serial broken into episodes.

clue.text: American saw evidence of deterioration after doing exercises, pathetic

indicators.note: after places the deterioration piece behind the others in the answer
to exercise something is to work it about, so the letters of the word doing are put through their paces into a new order

parts.note: pathetic in the sense of feeble is wet in British slang
rust is what shows that iron is deteriorating

explanation.surface: Someone notices the rot setting in after a feeble workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' is the anagram signal working on 'doing', not a gym word; 'after' puts the deterioration piece at the end. 'Wet' as feeble is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a saying or motto, and this one is the official motto of the United States, printed on its money.

clue.text: Assuming elected, hold down a cushy job

indicators.note: to assume something is to take it on board, so the hold-down piece takes the elected piece inside it

parts.note: to hold something down is to secure it
someone elected is in office, IN

explanation.surface: Once voted in, hang on to an easy number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assuming' reads as 'supposing' but is the container signal: the hold-down word takes the elected one inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post with pay but little or no work, the classic undemanding position.

clue.text: See 21
High street retailer once seeing value in a fabric?

parts.note: wool is a fabric
value means worth

explanation.surface: A former shop chain is said to see value in a textile.
explanation.walkthrough: The '?' points to reading the shop's name as 'wool worth', the value found in a fabric. Woolworths was a British high street chain that closed in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolworth's was a famous chain store on British main shopping streets until it went under in 2008.

clue.text: Little growth in industry initially, while privileged type stuck up

indicators.note: in a down entry, stuck up says the letters are read from the bottom upwards
initially says only the opening letter of industry is used

parts.note: while in the sense of during the time that is as
a nob is a toff, a privileged person

explanation.surface: Industry grows only a little while the posh, stuck-up types prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck up' looks like snobbery but reverses IASNOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonsai is a tree kept deliberately miniature, so a small plant.

clue.text: One in unfamiliar surroundings, as 21 5?

definitions.meaning: a person out of their element, ill at ease in a strange place
read 21 5 as a fish that has left its school, i.e. its shoal, and so is out of the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 21 5 is SCHOOL-LEAVER; a school is also a group of fish, so one leaving it is pictured as stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone awkward in an unfamiliar setting, like a stranded creature gasping on land.

clue.text: Wide containers, four in river

indicators.note: in puts the containers and the four inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
pans are cooking containers
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Broad vessels, four of them, floating in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something expansive covers a large area, so it is broad or extensive.

clue.text: Batting sides interrupted

definitions.meaning: in cricket the two halves of the field either side of the batsman are the on side and the off side

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the on (leg) side and the off side relative to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An on-off relationship or signal keeps stopping and restarting, which is intermittent.

clue.text: Sooner at sea, hard to be kept — away from it?

indicators.note: something kept is held within, so the hard piece is put inside the jumbled letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of Sooner are scrambled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A sailor would rather be at sea, keeping things hard, than away from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' scrambles SOONER into ONSORE, which keeps H inside. 'it' in the definition is the sea of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: On land by the coast is away from the sea, which the 'it' refers back to.

clue.text: More than one case exists in glens

indicators.note: in puts the exists piece inside the glens

parts.note: glens are valleys, vales
exists means is

explanation.surface: There is more than one example to be found in the valleys.
explanation.definitionFit: Valises are small travelling bags, so several suitcases.

clue.text: Man, failure heading for extinction

parts.note: a dud is a failure

indicators.note: heading for means the opening letter of extinction

explanation.surface: Mankind, a flop, is on its way to dying out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude is slang for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Ornate picture frames or nothing in US territory

indicators.note: a frame goes around a picture, so the scrambled letters surround the next word
ornate means elaborately worked, so the letters of picture are rearranged

parts.note: O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A gilded painting is hung in an American overseas holding, or perhaps nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ornate' turns PICTURE into PUERTIC, which 'frames' OR; then O for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerto Rico is a Caribbean island that is an unincorporated territory of the United States.

clue.text: Individual club sandwiches toward the mouth?

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to put it in the middle, so the club piece surrounds the individual piece

parts.note: a driver is a golf club
individual means one's own, OWN

explanation.surface: Someone's club sandwich heads for their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club sandwiches' looks like food, but the club is a golf club and 'sandwiches' is the container signal. The mouth is a river's, not a person's.
explanation.definitionFit: Going downstream means moving toward where a river meets the sea, the mouth of a river.

clue.text: Old song lyric contested by a number in the south of France?

definitions.text: Old song lyric contested by a number in the south of France?

parts.words: Old song lyric contested by a number in the south of France?
parts.note: the chant was sung by football fans, and '...' could be read as a number one in Nice, a city of southern France

explanation.walkthrough: The 1973 song chanted for Tottenham Hotspur's Cyril Knowles; 'a number in the south of France' is a playful reading of its first two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was the hook of a 1973 football chart hit praising Spurs defender Cyril Knowles.

clue.text: See 3
Buckinghamshire town upset different town in Kent

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: something different is new
Dover is a port town in Kent, England

explanation.surface: One English town is upset by another rival town down in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like emotion but reverses NEW; Wendover is a small town in Buckinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Wendover is a market town in the Chiltern Hills of Buckinghamshire.

clue.text: American sport on the rise, game not half taking over

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up

parts.note: RU is short for Rugby Union

indicators.note: not half says only one half of the game's name is kept

parts.note: ping-pong is table tennis

explanation.surface: An American sport is booming, while some game is half pushed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rise' reverses RU to UR; 'not half' drops PONG from PINGPONG.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurping means seizing a position or power belonging to another.

clue.text: Instrument, on which I produce notes, is running

parts.note: an organ is a musical instrument
to sing is to produce musical notes

explanation.surface: A musician explains the instrument on which they play notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' looks musical-neutral but is the definition, in the sense of managing.
explanation.definitionFit: Running an event means managing or arranging it.

clue.text: 8, perhaps? One's smoked

definitions.meaning: the stranded creature of 8 is pictured gulping for air, so it is one that pants
a British slang term for a cheap cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: 8 is A FISH OUT OF WATER, which gasps for breath. A gasper is old British slang for a cheap cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette is something smoked, and a stranded fish is one that gulps air.

clue.text: Serve alcohol in a quandary — might one be 16 or 18?

indicators.note: being in a quandary means being muddled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone is in a dilemma over whether to serve drink to a teenager who might be 16 or 18.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a quandary' scrambles SERVEALCOHOL. In Britain pupils can finish school at 16 or carry on to 18.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils in Britain finish their education at 16 or 18, so either age fits a person finishing school.

clue.text: Pudding failed

definitions.meaning: a ... is a boiled suet pudding, as in plum ...
... in British slang means broken or useless

explanation.definitionFit: Plum duff is a steamed suet dessert, and British slang calls something broken or useless duff.

clue.text: See 16
Argentine trained to shoot Admiral Horatio primarily, as Lord

parts.note: Lionel Messi is the Argentine footballer, a trained goal scorer

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of each of these words

explanation.surface: An Argentine marksman takes aim at Nelson, revered almost as a lord.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Horatio Nelson suggests a naval battle, but only his initials are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians call Jesus both Lord and the Messiah, the anointed saviour.

clue.text: In Greece, plain old folly ultimately, politician inspired by cheat no end

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so the trimmed cheat takes the next letters inside
no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a liar is a cheat

indicators.note: ultimately means the last letter of folly

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An old Greek folly sees a politician take his inspiration from a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' trims the cheat to LIA; 'inspired by' then puts both the last letter of folly and the politician inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympia is the plain in the western Peloponnese where the ancient Olympic Games were held.

clue.text: Relative seen from behind in codpiece, inconsolable

indicators.note: seen from behind says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A family member, spotted from the rear wearing a codpiece, is in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside the words 'codpiece, inconsolable' and run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: As soon as guards happen to fade away, that's submission

indicators.note: guards means surrounds protectively, so the first piece holds the others

parts.note: once in the sense of as soon as
to be means to take place, happen
to die away is to fade

explanation.surface: Once the guards let things fade away, they submit.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is compliance or yielding to authority, a form of submission.
